so.subjective:
* The patient reports that their knee feels loose and unstable, allowing them to still walk, but with decreased stability.
* The patient is a 32-year-old male who injured his right knee three days ago while playing soccer. He reported a sudden pop on the inside of his knee while attempting to plank kick the ball. He described the pain as a 6 or 7 out of 10, which makes walking uncomfortable. He experiences tenderness on the inside of his knee, especially when pressed, and has difficulty bending or straightening his knee without discomfort.
* The patient has no prior history of knee issues or surgeries.
* The patient reports that the tenderness has been uncomfortable, but not as bad as it was initially.
* He has not experienced any numbness or tingling in his leg since the injury.
* He has not noticed any clicking, popping, or locking sensations in his knee when moving it.
* He has not experienced any previous episodes of knee instability or injury.
* The patient denies having undergone any imaging studies, such as X-rays or MRI, for this injury.

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I'm 32 years old, and I'm male. I came in because I injured my right knee about three days ago while playing soccer, and it's been swollen and not moving as well as it used to. It's been pretty painful, and I can't really bend or straighten it fully without some discomfort.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Can you describe the mechanism of injury in more detail? For example, did you twist your knee, land awkwardly, or collide with another player?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I was trying to plank kick the ball, and I just felt a pop in my right knee. I didn't really twist it or collide with anyone, it just happened when I made that move.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any instability, locking, or a sensation of the knee giving way since the injury? Additionally, have you had any prior history of knee issues, such as previous injuries, surgeries, or chronic conditions?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't experienced any instability or the knee giving way, but it does feel loose and doesn't move normally. I don't have any prior history of knee issues or surgeries.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you undergone any imaging studies such as X-rays or MRI for this injury, and if so, what were the findings?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had any imaging studies done yet. The doctor mentioned they're going to order an MRI to check the integrity of my ACL, but that's going to happen after this visit.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Can you describe the exact location of the pop in your knee and whether there was any associated sound or sensation at the time of injury?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The pop was on the inside of my knee, and I didn't really hear anything specific, but it just felt like something gave way when I made that move. It was pretty sudden.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Can you describe the current level of pain on a scale from 1 to 10, and how it affects your ability to walk or perform daily activities? Also, have you noticed any bruising or tenderness in specific areas of your knee?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The pain is around a 6 or 7 right now, and it makes walking uncomfortable. I can still walk on it, but it feels really loose and unstable. I don’t have much bruising, but there’s some tenderness on the inside of my knee, especially when the doctor pressed on it. It’s been hard to do things like sit for long periods or move my leg without some discomfort.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you noticed any clicking, popping, or locking sensations in your knee when moving it, and have you experienced any numbness or tingling in your leg?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't noticed any clicking or locking sensations in my knee when moving it, and I haven't had any numbness or tingling in my leg. It just feels loose and unstable, especially when I try to bend or straighten it.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any previous episodes of knee instability or injury, even if they were minor?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I don't think so. I haven't had any previous issues with my knee feeling unstable or injured before this. This is the first time I've experienced anything like this.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Can you describe the exact moment of the pop in your knee during the soccer incident? Was there any specific movement or contact that caused it?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I was trying to plank kick the ball, and when I made that movement, I felt a sudden pop on the inside of my knee. It happened pretty quickly, and I didn’t really have any contact with another player or anything like that—it just felt like something gave way when I made that move.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you experienced any numbness or tingling in your leg since the injury?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't experienced any numbness or tingling in my leg since the injury. It's just been the pain, swelling, and the feeling of instability in my knee. Everything else feels normal.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Can you describe the exact movement you were making when you felt the pop in your knee? Also, have you noticed any locking or catching sensations in your knee since the injury?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I was trying to plank kick the ball, so I was kind of bending my knee and pushing off the ground to kick it, and that's when I felt the pop. And no, I haven't noticed any locking or catching sensations in my knee since the injury. It just feels loose and unstable, especially when I try to bend or straighten it.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe the exact location of the tenderness on your knee and whether you've noticed any changes in the way your knee feels over the past three days?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The tenderness is on the inside of my knee, near the joint line. Over the past three days, it's been getting a little better with the swelling going down, but the knee still feels unstable and weak, especially when I try to move it fully. It's been pretty uncomfortable, but not as bad as it was at first.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe any specific activities or movements that make the instability or weakness in your knee worse? Have you noticed any changes in the way your knee feels over the past few days?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The instability and weakness in my knee seem to get worse when I try to bend it fully or straighten it, especially if I put any weight on it. It feels like it's not holding up properly, and I have to use my hand to help straighten it sometimes. Over the past few days, the swelling has gone down a bit, but the feeling of looseness and instability is still there. It's been uncomfortable, but not as bad as it was at first.
